correctness.rationale: Exact two-by-two observation matrix factorization implies a strictly earlier optimal first event under each of D/A/E; for fixed gap the larger row-trace and positive shift factor strictly lower E information, increase A inverse trace and decrease D determinant. At first time zero, one-variable D and A derivatives yield unique normalized delays 1 and c=1+W(2e^{-2})/2. The E criterion is the smaller positive eigenvalue of a two-row Gramian. Its characteristic derivative has the same sign as 1+rho^2*d*(d-1)-exp(2d)*(d-1) for d>1; G(d)=exp(2d)/d-1/[d(d-1)] strictly increases from zero at c to infinity, yielding unique z_rho>c. A finite horizon clips each unique optimizer. The limiting value and asymptotic expansions follow by substitution and inverse-function expansion. Actual verification/check.py ran 6 symbolic identities and 117600 finite direct-design comparisons; the continuous proof is algebraic and does not rely on sample exhaustion.

value.rationale: Two independent scalar observations are the minimal cardinality for finite Fisher information on both initial coordinates of the nonnormal two-state Jordan system. The three standard D/A/E criteria provably select three distinct globally unique time clocks when the horizon permits, explaining a concrete design tradeoff. The A clock is independent of shear but the E clock increases logarithmically with shear, a substantive structural law useful to noise-sensitive observation timing. The complete natural classification is stronger than isolated arithmetic values and is not a routine direct corollary of the known pinned three-event determinant result. It is limited to equal event weights and specified coordinates; no claims for general matrices or accuracy are made.
